omitted_intervals: unmeasured external telephony, provider network, and remote playback intervals
omitted_gateway_owned_intervals: WebSocketTelephonyMediaAdapter._inbound_queue residence time before bridge pops it
producer queue.put backpressure wait (t_enqueued - t_pre_enqueue) under queue saturation
local ASGI websocket.send_bytes await duration (tracked separately as network_transport_ms)
ASGI server framework demuxing, routing, and task-switch latency
omitted_external_intervals: telephony carrier / PSTN / SIP network propagation wire delay
client OS TCP network stack and kernel socket buffer queueing
upstream AI provider network round-trip, model inference, and audio synthesis
remote endpoint jitter buffering, audio hardware decoding, and physical acoustic playback
gateway_added_overhead_estimate_ms.note: Descriptive heuristic sum of marginal component percentiles across in_proc + out_proc + in_q_wait + out_q_wait. This sum of marginal percentiles is NOT the true p95 of the conjoint Gateway transit distribution, is NOT a statistically guaranteed upper bound (which is mathematically false when tail events are disjoint), and omits both Gateway-owned and external latency intervals. It cannot by itself certify compliance with NFR-PERF-004.

limitations: Loopback WebSocket synthetic echo RTT measures local client-to-Gateway-to-FakeAI-to-client transfer on 127.0.0.1, NOT production PSTN/RTP network latency or AI model inference time.

Upstream AI generation latency (upstream_ai_generation_ms), external telephony network latency (external_telephony_network_ms), and remote speaker playback latency (remote_playback_latency_ms) are unmeasured in synthetic mode and reported as available=False / None.
Windows and non-RT OS schedulers exhibit timer wakeup granularity (~1-15.6 ms), which directly affects client send scheduling lateness and event-loop sleep probes without indicating Gateway blocking.
NFR-PERF-004 (p95 Gateway-added overhead <= 50 ms) is evaluated as a design target on the local reference environment, not a production SLA guarantee.
python_heap_peak_kib is measured via stdlib tracemalloc (Python allocator heap) and is distinct from OS process RSS (process_rss_peak_kib).
